    fix(v4): enforce the six JSON Schema keywords fromJSONSchema silently dropped (#6535)
    
    * fix(v4): enforce the six JSON Schema keywords fromJSONSchema silently dropped
    
    `minProperties`/`maxProperties` fold into the pre-pipe guard that already enforces `propertyNames`, so they count the raw input's own keys. `uniqueItems` and `contains`/`minContains`/`maxContains` run as checks on the converted array schema, with structural equality for duplicates. All six are carried into metadata like `propertyNames`, so `toJSONSchema` round-trips them.
    
    No public API and no file outside from-json-schema.ts, so mini and non-users pay nothing.
    
    Closes #6463
    
    * fix: evaluate the array keywords on the raw instance, pre-pipe
    
    `uniqueItems` and the `contains` family moved into a pre-pipe guard mirroring `checkObjectGuards`: a nested `default` in `items` made the post-parse checks accept a `contains` the instance fails and reject distinct items as duplicates. The property-count issues carry explicit messages, since no locale has a Sizable entry for `object`.
    
    * test: pin the two side effects of the pre-pipe guards
    
    A guard issue aborts the pipe, so `minItems`/`maxItems` are not co-reported, and the guard's identity transform makes `toJSONSchema` strip `default`/`examples` from the input-mode document. Both are the cost of evaluating the keywords against the raw instance; recording them as tests so they read as deliberate.
    
    * perf: detect uniqueItems duplicates by canonical key instead of pairwise
    
    The pairwise deep-equal scan was quadratic on the parse path: an all-distinct array of 4,000 objects cost 246ms, and nothing bounds the length a converted schema accepts. Each element now hashes to an injective string, so detection is a Map lookup — the same array costs 5ms, and 20,000 elements cost 22ms where the old scan would have taken seconds. A cycle or a NaN, neither expressible in JSON, yields no key and is never called a duplicate; the old comparison would have recursed forever on the cycle.
    
    * fix: short-circuit the contains scan and drop carried subschemas that cannot resolve
    
    `contains` now stops one past `maxContains`, since nothing above the ceiling changes the verdict; the message for that direction no longer names a count it stopped measuring. A carried `contains` or `propertyNames` travels without the root `$defs` its `$ref`s point into, so one holding a reference is dropped rather than re-emitted as a dangling pointer in an otherwise valid document.
    
    * fix: do not read a $ref key inside instance data as a schema reference
    
    `default`, `const`, `enum` and `examples` hold instance data, where `$ref` is an ordinary property name. Descending into them made the carry drop a `contains` or `propertyNames` that was perfectly resolvable, widening the emitted schema.
    
    * fix: walk only schema positions when looking for a carried $ref
    
    Excluding the four standard instance keywords still left every unknown annotation traversed, so an `x-` extension holding a `$ref` key dropped a constraint that resolves. Inverted to an allowlist of the positions a schema can actually occupy.
    
    * fix: walk draft-7 dependencies when looking for a carried $ref

    fix(v4): fold an intersection of object schemas into one object (#6461)
    
    `z.toJSONSchema()` emits `z.intersection(A, B)` as `allOf: [A, B]`. `additionalProperties` in an `allOf` member only sees that member's own `properties`, so two closed object members reject each other's keys and no object validates — while the parser accepts them. The exporter contradicts itself.
    
    The parser already says what the answer is. `handleIntersectionResults` pools the members' key sets: a key is reported as unrecognized only when every side rejects it. So an intersection is closed exactly when every member is closed, over the union of their keys — which is a single object, and is what the intersection means.
    
    `finalize` folds it there, after `extractDefs`, so a member already extracted into `$defs` is a `$ref` by then and keeps its reference instead of being inlined. The member test is a whitelist of the four object keywords, so anything it does not understand — a `$ref`, `patternProperties`, an annotation — leaves the `allOf` exactly as it is today rather than dropping a constraint.
    
    Closes #5390.
